name: Titanium.UI.TableView
summary:
A table view is used to present information, organized in sections and rows, in a
vertically-scrolling view.
description:
| Android | iOS |
| ------- | --- |
| ![Android](./tableview_android.png) | ![iOS](./tableview_ios.png) |

A `TableView` object is a container for [TableViewSection](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewSection)
objects that are, in turn, containers for [TableViewRow](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow) objects.

Use the [Titanium.UI.createTableView](api:Titanium.UI#createTableView) method or **`<TableView>`** Alloy element to create a `TableView`.

Also see the [TableViews guide](https://titaniumsdk.com/guide/Titanium_SDK/Titanium_SDK_How-tos/User_Interface_Deep_Dives/TableViews.html).

#### Creating Tables

There are few approaches to creating and using `TableView` object.

The simplest approach is to pass dictionaries of `TableViewRow` properties, such as
[backgroundColor](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#backgroundColor),
[color](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#color), and [title](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#title), to the
[createTableView](api:Titanium.UI#createTableView) method, which causes the rows to be implicitly
created, added to a single [TableViewSection](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewSection), and then added to
the `TableView`. Refer to the "Simple Table View with Basic Rows" example.

For more control over the layout of each row, however, [TableViewRow](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow)
objects can be created explicitly using the [Titanium.UI.createTableViewRow](api:Titanium.UI#createTableViewRow) method. Child views,
such as [labels](api:Titanium.UI.Label), [images](api:Titanium.UI.ImageView), and
[buttons](api:Titanium.UI.Button), may be added to each row. When one or more
[rows](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow) are added to the table view,
a single [TableViewSection](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewSection) is automatically created to hold the
rows. See the "Table View with Composite Layout" example.

Lastly, sets of rows may be explicitly created and added to a their own
[TableViewSection](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewSection) objects, which are then added to a `TableView`,
to enable the rows to be organized. Headers and footers titles or views must be configured
in order for the sections to be visible.

#### Tables and Scroll Views

As a table view inherently scrolls, it creates a very poor user experience when one contains
other scrolling views, such as a [ScrollableView](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollableView) or
[TextArea](api:Titanium.UI.TextArea). Thus, this layout is strongly discouraged.

#### TextFields in Tables with SOFT_INPUT_ADJUST_PAN (Android)

When a [TextField](api:Titanium.UI.TextField) is placed in a row near the bottom of a `TableView`,
in a window that is configured with
[SOFT_INPUT_ADJUST_PAN](api:Titanium.UI.Android#SOFT_INPUT_ADJUST_PAN), it is expected for the
text field to automatically move to a visible position after it is focused and the software
keyboard displayed. However, due to a known problem caused by native Android's ListView behavior,
the keyboard is likely to completely obscure the text field.

To mitigate this, a `ScrollView` may be used instead of a table view, as demonstrated in the
[ScrollView](api:Titanium.UI.ScrollView), "Scroll View as a Table View", example.

#### Row Editing and Moving Modes

Table views have an `editing` and a `moving` mode that may be activated to using their
respective [editing](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#editing) and [moving](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#moving)
properties. These allow rows to be deleted or re-ordered by the user, depending on each row's
[editable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#editable) and [moveable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#moveable)
property that are either explicitly set or inherited from the table.

There are two UI controls available for deleting table view rows, depending on the combination
of editing and moving modes enabled:

* "red icon delete" - a circular red icon is displayed on the left-hand side of a row, which
reveals a delete button on the right-hand side of that row when clicked.
* "swipe delete" - without either of the table editing or moving modes enabled, a left or right
swipe gesture on a row reveals a delete button on the right-hand side of the row.

Note that because the operating system handles the functionality of the swipe delete, the OS will
capture swipe events and not bubble the event to Titanium listeners. As such, if you rely on
swipe events, you must not set editing to true on such rows, and simulate the functionality you
need.

When `editable` and `moveable` properties are set on the table view, they are known as `inherited`,
whereas when set on a row, they are known as `explicit`. As their resulting behavior may not
follow their literal meaning, depending on the combination of `editing` and `moving` modes that
are enabled, a detailed description of the behavior follows.

With `editing:false` and `moving:true`:

* For red icon delete and swipe delete, inherited and explicit `editable` properties may be set.
* Inherited `moveable` property is always `true`. Explicit `moveable` property may be set.

With `editing:true` and `moving:false`:

* For red icon delete and swipe delete, inherited `editable` property is always `true`. Explicit
`editable` property may be set.
* Inherited and explicit `moveable` properties may be set.

With `editing:false` and `moving: false`:

* For red icon delete, inherited and explicit `editable` properties always `false`. For
swipe delete, inherited and explicit `editable` properties may be set.
* Inherited `moveable` property is always `false`.

With `editing:true` and `moving:true`:

* For red icon delete and swipe delete, inherited and explicit `editable` properties may be set.
* Inherited `moveable` property is always `true`. Explicit `moveable` property may be set.

examples.title: Simple Table View
Table View Sections
Table View with Composite Layout
Alloy XML Markup
examples.code:
Previous table view sections example as an Alloy view.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <Window id="win">
        <TableView id="table">
            <TableViewSection id="sectionFruit" headerTitle="Fruit">
                <TableViewRow title="Apple"/>
                <TableViewRow title="Bananas"/>
            </TableViewSection>
            <TableViewSection id="sectionVeg" headerTitle="Vegetables">
                <TableViewRow title="Carrots"/>
                <TableViewRow title="Potatoes"/>
            </TableViewSection>
            <TableViewSection id="sectionFish" headerTitle="Fish">
                <TableViewRow title="Cod"/>
                <TableViewRow title="Haddock"/>
            </TableViewSection>
        </TableView>
    </Window>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: allowsMultipleSelectionDuringEditing
properties.summary: Determines whether multiple items of this table view can be selected at the same time while editing the table.

properties.name: allowsMultipleSelectionInteraction
properties.summary: Allows a two-finger pan gesture to automatically transition the table view into editing mode and start selecting rows.
properties.description:
Setting this property to true allows the user to start selecting multiple contiguous rows via a two-finger pan gesture.
If the table view is already in editing mode, the user can also select multiple rows via a one-finger pan gesture along
the edge of the table that contains editing controls (checkboxes). In order to support this behavior,
you must also set [Titanium.UI.TableView.allowsMultipleSelectionDuringEditing](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#allowsMultipleSelectionDuringEditing) to true.
Once user interaction stops the [Titanium.UI.TableView.rowsselected](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#rowsselected) event is fired.

properties.name: allowsSelection
properties.summary: Determines whether this table's rows can be selected.
properties.description: Set to `false` to prevent rows from being selected.

properties.name: allowsSelectionDuringEditing
properties.summary: Determines whether this table's rows can be selected while editing the table.
properties.description: Set to `true` to allow rows to be selected.

properties.name: backgroundColor
properties.summary: Background color of the view, as a color name or hex triplet.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).
properties.default: transparent on non-iOS platforms, white on the iOS platform

properties.name: contentOffset
properties.summary: X and Y coordinates to which to reposition the top-left point of the content region.

properties.name: data
properties.summary: Rows of the table view.

properties.name: dimBackgroundForSearch
properties.summary: A Boolean indicating whether the underlying content is dimmed during a search.
properties.description:
If you do not want to show the dimmed background when clicking on the search bar,
set this property `false` during creation.

properties.name: editable
properties.summary:
Determines the rows' default editable behavior, which allows them to be deleted by the user
when the table is in `editing` or `moving` mode.
properties.description:
This property determines the default behavior of child rows, but may be overridden by
a row's [editable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#editable) property.

See the [Titanium.UI.TableView](api:Titanium.UI.TableView) description section for a full explanation of the TableView's
`editing` and `moving` modes.

properties.name: editing
properties.summary: Determines whether row editing mode is active.
properties.description:
The `editing` mode allows rows to be deleted or re-ordered, depending on their
[editable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#editable) and [moveable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#moveable)
settings.

See the [Titanium.UI.TableView](api:Titanium.UI.TableView) description section for a full explanation of the TableView's
`editing` and `moving` modes.

properties.name: filterAnchored
properties.summary: Determines whether the search is limited to the start of the string
properties.description: Set to `true` to enable case anchored search.

properties.name: filterAttribute
properties.summary: Filter attribute to be used when searching.
properties.description:
On the Android platform, this property can only be set to Titanium-defined properties of the
TableViewRow object, such as `title`.  To search text stored in a different attribute, set the `title`
property of the TableViewRow object to the property to be searched. For example:

``` js
var label = Ti.UI.createLabel({text: 'Foobar'}),
var row = Ti.UI.createTableViewRow(title: label.text);
row.add(label);
```

On the iOS platform, this property can be set to any property on the TableViewRow object,
including arbitrary properties set on the object, not only Titanium-defined properties.

Note that the filter is not anchored to the beginning of the string. So typing "ha"
in the text box will include rows titled 'Harold' and 'Harvard', but also 'Sharon'
and 'Jonathan'.

properties.name: filterCaseInsensitive
properties.summary: Determines whether the search is case insensitive.
properties.description: Set to `false` to enable case sensitive search.

properties.name: fixedSize
properties.summary: Sets fixedSize mode on Android TableView.
properties.description: Set it to `true` if all TableView items have the same size to gain some performance.

properties.name: footerDividersEnabled
properties.summary: When set to false, the ListView will not draw the divider before the footer view.

properties.name: footerTitle
properties.summary: Table view footer title.

properties.name: footerView
properties.summary: Table view footer as a view that will be rendered instead of a label.
properties.description:
In Alloy you can use a `<FooterView>` element nested in a `<TableView>` element:

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <TableView>
        <FooterView>
            <View backgroundColor="#a00" height="50dp"/>
        </FooterView>
        <TableViewRow><Label>Row 1</Label></TableViewRow>
        <TableViewRow><Label>Row 2</Label></TableViewRow>
    </TableView>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: headerDividersEnabled
properties.summary: When set to false, the ListView will not draw the divider after the header view.

properties.name: headerPullView
properties.summary:
View positioned above the first row that is only revealed when the user drags the table
contents down.
properties.description:
A `headerPullView` is a UI control that is often used to provide a convenient way for the
user to refresh a table's data.  Typically used with the
[setContentInsets](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#setContentInsets) method.

To specify the wrapper color see [Titanium.UI.View.pullBackgroundColor](api:Titanium.UI.View#pullBackgroundColor).

For an example, see the "Pull to refresh" section in the
[TableViews guide](https://titaniumsdk.com/guide/Titanium_SDK/Titanium_SDK_How-tos/User_Interface_Deep_Dives/TableViews.html).

Alloy applications can use a `<HeaderPullView>` element inside a `<TableView>` element.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <TableView>
        <HeaderPullView platform="ios">
            <View class="pull">
                <Label color="#F2F4F4" bottom="25dp">Header pull view</Label>
            </View>
        </HeaderPullView>
    </TableView>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: headerTitle
properties.summary: Table view header title.

properties.name: headerView
properties.summary: Table view header as a view that will be rendered instead of a label.
properties.description:
In Alloy you can use a `<HeaderView>` element nested in a `<TableView>` element:

``` js
<Alloy>
    <TableView>
        <HeaderView>
            <View backgroundColor="#a00" height="50dp"/>
        </HeaderView>
        <TableViewRow><Label>Row 1</Label></TableViewRow>
        <TableViewRow><Label>Row 2</Label></TableViewRow>
    </TableView>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: hideSearchOnSelection
properties.summary: Determines whether the search field should hide on completion.
properties.description:
Set to `false` to prevent the search field from being hidden when an item in the search
results is clicked.

Many standard applications (such as Contacts) have a behavior equivalent to `false` for this
value, but the default is `true` for legacy reasons.

The Android platform behaves as though this value were `false`.

properties.name: index
properties.summary: Array of objects (with `title` and `index` properties) to control the table view index.
properties.description:
If an index array is specified, an index bar is displayed on the right-hand side of the
table view. Clicking on a title in the index bar scrolls the table view to the row
index associated with that title. If the index is -1 the table view will scroll to the top.

inlined.name: TableViewIndexEntry
inlined.summary: A simple object that represents an index entry in a `TableView`.

properties.name: index
properties.summary: Row index associated with this item.

properties.name: title
properties.summary: Title to display in the index bar for this item.

properties.name: keyboardDismissMode
properties.summary: The manner in which the keyboard is dismissed when a drag begins in the table view.

properties.name: maxClassname
properties.summary: Max number of row class names.
properties.description:
See [Titanium.UI.TableViewRow.className](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#className) for more details. This property will default to
32 when it is set to a number lesser than that.

properties.name: maxRowHeight
properties.summary: Maximum row height for table view rows.

properties.name: minRowHeight
properties.summary: Minimum row height for table view rows.

properties.name: moveable
properties.summary:
Determines the rows' default moveable behavior, which allows them to be re-ordered by the
user when the table is in `editing` or `moving` mode.
properties.description:
This property determines the default behavior of child rows, but may be overridden by a
row's [moveable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#moveable) property.

See the [Titanium.UI.TableView](api:Titanium.UI.TableView) description section for a full explanation of the TableView's
`editing` and `moving` modes.

properties.name: moving
properties.summary: Determines whether row moving mode is active.
properties.description:
The `moving` mode allows rows to be deleted or re-ordered, depending on their
[editable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#editable) and [moveable](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow#moveable)
settings.

See the [Titanium.UI.TableView](api:Titanium.UI.TableView) description section for a full explanation of the TableView's
`editing` and `moving` modes.

properties.name: overScrollMode
properties.summary: Determines the behavior when the user overscrolls the view.

properties.name: refreshControl
properties.summary: View positioned above the first row that is only revealed when the user drags the list view contents down.
properties.description: An alternate to the headerPullView property. See [Titanium.UI.RefreshControl](api:Titanium.UI.RefreshControl) for usage and examples.

properties.name: resultsBackgroundColor
properties.summary: The background color of the search results (iOS-only).
properties.description:
For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).
Note: A transparent background-color is not officially supported by Apple to
prevent that the list of results overlaps with the list view below it.

properties.name: resultsSeparatorColor
properties.summary:
Separator line color between rows inside search results,
as a color name or hex triplet (iOS-only).
properties.description:
To make the line invisible, set this property to `transparent`, or the same value as the
[backgroundColor](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#backgroundColor) property.
For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: resultsSeparatorInsets
properties.summary: The insets for search results separators (applies to all cells & iOS-only).
properties.description:
Cell separators do not extend all the way to the edge of the list view.
This property sets the default inset for all cells in the table.
Set this to a dictionary with two keys, `left` specifying inset from left edge and `right`
specifying the inset from the right edge.

properties.name: resultsSeparatorStyle
properties.summary: The separator style of the search results (iOS-only).

properties.name: rowHeight
properties.summary: Default row height for table view rows.

properties.name: rowSeparatorInsets
properties.summary: The insets for table view cells (applies to all cells).

properties.name: scrollable
properties.summary: If `true`, the table view can be scrolled.

properties.name: scrollIndicatorStyle
properties.summary: Style of the scrollbar.

properties.name: scrollsToTop
properties.summary: Controls whether the scroll-to-top gesture is effective.
properties.description:
The scroll-to-top gesture is a tap on the status bar; The default value of this property is true.
This gesture works when you have a single visible table view.
If there are multiple table views, web views, text areas, and/or scroll views visible,
you will need to disable (set to false) on the above views you DON'T want this
behaviour on. The remaining view will then respond to scroll-to-top gesture.

properties.name: search
properties.summary: Search field to use for the table view.
properties.description:
In an Alloy application, you can use a `<SearchView>` or `<SearchBar>` element inside a `<TableView>` element.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <TableView>
      <!-- search, shorthand with Ti.UI.SearchBar -->
      <SearchBar platform="ios"/>
      <!-- search, shorthand with Ti.UI.Android.SearchView -->
      <SearchView ns="Ti.UI.Android" platform="android"/>
    </TableView>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: searchAsChild
properties.summary: Determines whether the [SearchBar](api:Titanium.UI.SearchBar) or [SearchView](api:Titanium.UI.Android.SearchView) appears as part of the TableView.
properties.description: Set to false if the search view will be displayed in the action bar.

properties.name: searchHidden
properties.summary: Determines whether the search field is visible.
properties.description: Set to `true` to hide the search field.

properties.name: sectionCount
properties.summary: Number of sections in this table view.

properties.name: sectionHeaderTopPadding
properties.summary: Padding above each section header.
properties.description: If not set or set to `-1`, it defaults to an automatic spacing determined by the system.

properties.name: sections
properties.summary: Sections of this table.
properties.description:
In Release 3.0, this property is read-only on Android.

Due to a known issue, TIMOB-12616, the `sections` property should not be used
for adding sections on iOS.

properties.name: separatorColor
properties.summary: Separator line color between rows, as a color name or hex triplet.
properties.description:
To make the line invisible, set this property to `transparent`, or the same value as the
[backgroundColor](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#backgroundColor) property.

For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: separatorInsets
properties.summary: The insets for table view separators (applies to all cells).

properties.name: separatorStyle
properties.summary: Separator style constant.

properties.name: showSearchBarInNavBar
properties.summary: A Boolean indicating whether search bar will be in navigation bar.
properties.description:
If you want to show the search bar in navigation bar, set this property `true` during creation.
Use the [Titanium.UI.Window.hidesSearchBarWhenScrolling](api:Titanium.UI.Window#hidesSearchBarWhenScrolling) property to control the visibility of the
searchbar when scrolling.

properties.name: showSelectionCheck
properties.summary: Determines whether the selection checkmark is displayed on selected rows.

properties.name: showVerticalScrollIndicator
properties.summary: Determines whether this table view displays a vertical scroll indicator.
properties.description: Set to `false` to hide the vertical scroll indicator.

properties.name: snapping
properties.summary: Determines whether rows snap into place when scrolling stops.
properties.description:
When set to `true`, the row closest to the centre of the view is aligned with that
centre once a scroll comes to rest, rather than the table stopping at an arbitrary
offset. This is most useful when every row fills the visible area.

On Android this is backed by a
[LinearSnapHelper](https://developer.android.com/reference/androidx/recyclerview/widget/LinearSnapHelper).
On iOS the equivalent behaviour is applied while the scroll decelerates. Snapping is
skipped when the resting position falls on a header or footer rather than a row.

properties.name: style
properties.summary:
Style of the table view, specified using one of the constants from
[Titanium.UI.iOS.TableViewStyle](api:Titanium.UI.iOS.TableViewStyle).
properties.description: Style should always be set before setting the `data` on table view.

properties.name: tableSeparatorInsets
properties.summary: The insets for the table view header and footer.

properties.name: touchFeedback
properties.summary: A material design visual construct that provides an instantaneous visual confirmation of touch point.
properties.description: Touch feedback is only applied to a view's background.

methods.name: appendRow
methods.summary: Appends a single row or an array of rows to the end of the table.
methods.description:
Each row can be passed as a [TableViewRow](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewRow) object, or as
dictionary specifying the properties for a table row, in which case this `TableView` will
create `TableViewRow` objects as needed.

On iOS, the row(s) can be inserted with animation by specifying a `properties` parameter.

parameters.name: row
parameters.summary: Row or rows to add to the table.

inlined.name: TableViewAnimationProperties
inlined.summary: A simple object for specifying the animation properties to use when inserting or deleting rows, or scrolling the table.
inlined.description:
Not all properties apply to all methods.

`animationStyle` does not apply to the `scrollToTop` or `scrollToIndex` methods.

`positon` only applies to the `scrollToIndex` method.

properties.name: animated
properties.summary: Whether this table change should be animated. Ignored if any `animationStyle` value is specified.

properties.name: animationStyle
properties.summary: Type of animation to use for row insertions and deletions.
properties.default:
If `animated` is `true` but no `animationStyle` is specified, the style defaults to
[FADE](Titanium.UI.iOS.RowAnimationStyle.FADE).

properties.name: position
properties.summary: Specifies what position to scroll the selected row to.

methods.name: appendSection
methods.summary: Appends a single section or an array of sections to the end of the table.
methods.description:
Each section can be passed as a [TableViewSection](api:Titanium.UI.TableViewSection) object, or as
dictionary specifying the properties for a table section, in which case this `TableView` will
create `TableViewSection` objects as needed.

On iOS, the section(s) can be inserted with animation by specifying a `properties` parameter.

Due to a known issue, TIMOB-12616, this method should not be used for adding sections on iOS.

parameters.summary: Section or section to add to the table.

methods.name: scrollToTop
methods.summary:
Scrolls the table to a specific top position where 0 is the topmost y position in the
table view.
methods.description:
The behavior of this method is platform-specific.

On Android, the `top` value is interpreted as a row index that should be scrolled
to the top of the screen. The table will not scroll the last row of data higher than
the bottom of the screen. If there is less than one screenful of data below the
specified row, the table doesn't scroll the specified row all the way to the top.
If the table has less than one screenful of data total, it does not scroll at all.

On iOS, the `top` value is interpreted as a pixel offset between the top of the top
row of data and the top of the table view. So a `top` value of 0 scrolls the list to
the top. A positive value scrolls it down, and a negative value scrolls the list up
above the first item.

On iOS, specify a [TableViewAnimationProperties](api:TableViewAnimationProperties) object with `animated` set to `false` to
disable the scrolling animation.

parameters.name: top
parameters.summary: Y position for the top of the table view.

methods.summary:
Programmatically selects a row. In Android, it sets the currently selected item. If in touch mode,
the item will not be selected but it will still be positioned appropriately. If the specified
selection position is less than 0, then the item at position 0 will be selected.

methods.name: setContentInsets
methods.description:
A table view is essentially a scroll view that contains a set of static row views that
represents the content. Thus, the `setContentInsets` method facilitates a margin, or inset,
distance between the content and the container scroll view.

Typically used with the [headerPullView](api:Titanium.UI.TableView#headerPullView) property.

parameters.name: edgeInsets
parameters.summary:
Sets the distance that the content view is inset from the enclosing scroll view of the table.
For example:

``` js
setContentInset({ top: 50, bottom: 10, right: 10, left: 10 }, { animated: true });
```

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary:
Determines whether, and how, the content inset change should be animated.

Note that the default here is equivalent to passing in `{ animated: false }`

methods.name: setContentOffset
methods.summary: Sets the value of the content offset of the table view without animation by default.

parameters.name: contentOffset
parameters.summary:
Dictionary with the properties `x`, `y`.
The `x` and `y` coordinates reposition the top-left point of the scrollable region of the table view.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary:
Pass in `{ animated: true }` to animate the transition.

Note that the default here is equivalent to passing in `{ animated: false }`
